options.B: Patients refuse to visit clinics that submit paperwork after the fifth day
options.C: It prevents nurses from taking their mandatory annual leave days
options.D: Late submissions disrupt national supply chain forecasting and drug distribution

explanation: National health planners rely on timely reports to distribute vaccines, drugs, and consumables where needed. [learn more](GNS124_U6_T2#GNS124_U6_T2_h5)

question: Why is skull traction applied before some neck surgeries?

options.A: To shrink swollen soft tissues around the wound
options.B: To clear bacterial infections from the spinal canal
options.C: To test if the patient is allergic to metal pins
options.D: To realign displaced bones into the correct position

explanation: Pre-operative traction pulls the spine straight so the surgeon has a better starting point for fusion. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T11#GNS221_U1_T11_h2)

question: Why does barium sulfate appear clearly on x-ray films?

options.A: It has a high atomic number
options.B: It emits radioactive gamma rays
options.C: It dissolves completely in blood plasma
options.D: It reacts with stomach acid to produce gas

explanation: Elements with high atomic numbers absorb x-rays much better than soft tissues, creating high contrast on the radiograph. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T14#GNS221_U2_T14_h1)

question: Why must a sputum sample be obtained from a deep cough rather than saliva?

options.A: To target material from the lower respiratory tract
options.B: To prevent the specimen from coagulating too quickly
options.C: To increase the overall volume of liquid collected
options.D: To eliminate all normal skin flora from the sample

explanation: Saliva contains mouth flora that do not represent the actual pathogen causing a lower respiratory infection. [learn more](GST114_U5_T4#GST114_U5_T4_h2)

question: What is the dark midline vertical line on the pregnant abdomen called?

options.A: Striae gravidarum
options.B: Chloasma
options.C: Spider angioma
options.D: Linea nigra

explanation: Linea nigra is the pigmented line that commonly develops down the center of the abdomen during pregnancy. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T9#GNS121_U7_T9_h2)

question: What term describes an abstract idea like pain or coping within a research framework?

options.A: A statistic
options.B: A concept
options.C: A hypothesis
options.D: An appendix

explanation: Concepts represent the abstract phenomena or ideas that researchers seek to study and understand within healthcare settings. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T11#GNS217_U3_T11_h3)

question: What is the primary characteristic of a healthcare team in the norming stage?

options.A: Achieving high clinical efficiency smoothly
options.B: Meeting for the very first time with politeness
options.C: Establishing rules and building mutual trust
options.D: Disbanding after completing a specific project

explanation: In the norming stage, members resolve earlier differences, agree on shared rules, and develop strong cooperative bonds. [learn more](GST321_U7_T1#GST321_U7_T1_h3)

question: A patient needs 1000 mL of normal saline infused over 8 hours using tubing with a drop factor of 15 gtt/mL. What parameter is being calculated?

options.A: The total daily fluid deficit of the client
options.B: The gravity flow rate in drops per minute
options.C: The total drug concentration in milligrams
options.D: The exact pressure inside the central vein

explanation: Volume, time, and drop factor are the variables used to find the drop rate per minute for gravity feeds. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T5#GNS125_U3_T5_h7)

question: Which infection is commonly associated with triggering an aplastic crisis in sickle cell patients?

options.A: Parvovirus B19
options.B: Plasmodium falciparum
options.C: Salmonella typhi
options.D: Mycobacterium tuberculosis

explanation: Parvovirus B19 specifically infects red blood cell precursors in the bone marrow, halting red cell production and causing an aplastic crisis. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T8#GNS313_U3_T8_h5)

question: How many times a day should a drug prescribed as TDS be administered?

options.A: Two times daily
options.B: Four times daily
options.C: Every twelve hours
options.D: Three times daily

explanation: The abbreviation TDS stands for ter in die, which translates to three times daily dosing. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T8#GNS125_U2_T8_h2)

question: What is an unsafe method for thawing frozen food items?

options.A: Leaving the food on a kitchen counter at room temperature
options.B: Using a microwave oven followed by immediate cooking
options.C: Placing the food inside a refrigerator operating at 4°C
options.D: Submerging the food package in continuous cold running water

explanation: Room temperature thawing leaves outer surfaces in the danger zone long before the center thaws, encouraging bacterial growth. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T009#GNS227_U3_T009_h6)

question: Poor waste management in a community most directly leads to what health issue?

options.A: Reduction in local market revenue
options.B: Decline in secondary school enrollment
options.C: Shortage of qualified teachers
options.D: Increased breeding of disease vectors

explanation: Accumulated refuse and poor sewage create breeding grounds for mosquitoes and other vectors transmitting infectious diseases. [learn more](GNS225_U1_T5#GNS225_U1_T5_h2)

question: Why is it important to define clear learning objectives before teaching a nursing seminar?

options.A: To satisfy administrative filing rules without actual teaching
options.B: To ensure the lecture runs for the maximum possible hours
options.C: To prevent participants from asking difficult clinical questions
options.D: To guide the selection of appropriate content and teaching methods

explanation: Clear objectives ensure that every part of the educational activity targets the intended knowledge or skill outcome. [learn more](GST321_U8_T8#GST321_U8_T8_h4)

question: Which challenge often threatens the long-term survival of NGO-run health projects?

options.A: Heavy reliance on unpredictable donor funding
options.B: Mandatory takeover by international military forces
options.C: Zero interest from local community members
options.D: An excessive surplus of trained medical doctors

explanation: Because NGOs depend on external grants and donations, their programs often struggle when funding streams dry up. [learn more](GNS123_U6_T6#GNS123_U6_T6_h6)

question: Why is reusing empty agrochemical containers for domestic water storage dangerous?

options.A: Toxic chemical residues can leach into the water and cause poisoning
options.B: Plastic containers degrade quickly when exposed to sunlight
options.C: It increases the growth of harmless algae inside the container
options.D: The water will change its natural color immediately

explanation: Chemical residues cling to plastic materials and cannot be easily washed out, contaminating any water stored inside later. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T13#GNS313_U3_T13_h7)

question: At what capacity should a sharps disposal container be closed and replaced?

options.A: One-quarter full
options.B: Completely packed to the brim
options.C: Whenever it starts to smell
options.D: Three-quarters full

explanation: Sharps containers must be sealed at 75% capacity to prevent accidental punctures when adding more items. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T10#GNS122_U3_T10_h5)

question: What term describes the complete absence of hydrochloric acid in gastric secretions?

options.A: Hyperemesis
options.B: Achlorhydria
options.C: Dyspepsia
options.D: Steatorrhea

explanation: Achlorhydria means the stomach mucosa fails to produce hydrochloric acid, often seen in pernicious anemia. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T3#GNS213_U3_T3_h6)

question: Why do healthcare workers often fail to report near-misses in clinical settings?

options.A: Fear of disciplinary action or punitive measures
options.B: Absence of sick leave for clinical personnel
options.C: Strict orders from the national nursing council
options.D: Lack of interest in patient safety improvement

explanation: A punitive work culture drives errors underground; staff will not report mistakes if they fear losing their jobs. [learn more](GST319_U4_T4#GST319_U4_T4_h5)

question: Why are complex proteins usually better antigens than simple lipids?

options.A: Proteins have more complex and varied structures for immune recognition
options.B: Lipids cannot enter the bloodstream under any circumstances
options.C: Proteins destroy white blood cells before they react
options.D: Simple lipids dissolve completely in body fluids instantly

explanation: Varied structural shapes allow immune cells to easily spot and bind to protein antigens compared to simpler molecules. [learn more](GST114_U4_T2#GST114_U4_T2_h1)

question: Needlestick injuries experienced by healthcare workers represent exposure to which hazard category?

options.A: Chemical hazards
options.B: Biological hazards
options.C: Ergonomic hazards
options.D: Physical hazards

explanation: Needlestick injuries transmit bloodborne pathogens, categorizing them as biological workplace hazards. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T6#GNS225_U7_T6_h4)

question: Which of these is NOT a primary prevention nursing action for adolescent injuries?

options.A: Advocating for community policies against youth substance sale
options.B: Conducting school seminars on peaceful conflict resolution
options.C: Educating students on road safety and helmet use
options.D: Applying a plaster cast to a fractured tibia

explanation: Applying a cast is a treatment intervention used after an injury has already happened. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T7#GNS312_U3_T7_h8)

question: Why do patients frequently stop taking their prescribed medications prematurely?

options.A: They prefer to take bitter traditional herbs instead
options.B: They feel better and assume the illness is completely cured
options.C: They receive daily phone calls from the hospital pharmacist
options.D: They have unlimited financial resources to buy more drugs

explanation: Symptom resolution often tricks patients into believing the treatment course is finished, leading to non-adherence especially with antibiotics. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T6#GNS215_U1_T6_h5)

question: What is the main difference between a disease reservoir and a disease source?

options.A: A reservoir is found in hospitals, while a source is in rural areas
options.B: A reservoir causes chronic illnesses, whereas a source causes acute infections
options.C: A reservoir is an inanimate object, while a source is an animal
options.D: A reservoir is where the agent naturally lives and multiplies, while a source is what directly infects the host

explanation: The reservoir provides the natural home for survival, while the source is the immediate point of transmission to the host. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T78#GNS214_U1_T78_h5)

question: What is polypharmacy?

options.A: The simultaneous use of multiple medications by a patient
options.B: The manufacturing of fake drugs in unlicensed factories
options.C: The practice of buying drugs from unregistered market vendors
options.D: The storage of expired medicines in a home cupboard

explanation: Polypharmacy refers to taking multiple medications concurrently, which raises the risk of adverse interactions. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T9#GNS223_U3_T9_h3)

question: A patient complains of sharp pain in the right lower abdominal quadrant. Which organ is most likely involved?

options.A: Appendix
options.B: Stomach
options.C: Spleen
options.D: Gallbladder

explanation: The appendix is typically located in the right lower quadrant, making it the primary organ suspected during localized pain in that area. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T3#GNS111_U1_T3_h5)

question: What is the primary source of psychological trauma following a major disaster?

options.A: Temporary relocation to urban centers
options.B: Lack of formal education on disasters
options.C: Pre-existing chronic physical illnesses
options.D: Sudden loss and extreme uncertainty

explanation: Trauma during disasters is primarily triggered by sudden disruptions, loss of life or property, and extreme uncertainty about safety. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T6#GNS315_U5_T6_h1)

question: Why must a single positive Widal test be read with care in areas where typhoid is common?

options.A: Blood samples degrade too quickly in tropical laboratory settings
options.B: Antibodies disappear entirely within hours of initial infection
options.C: Past infections or vaccinations leave permanent baseline antibodies in the blood
options.D: The test only detects viral particles instead of bacterial components

explanation: People living in endemic areas often carry baseline antibodies from previous exposures, which can cause false positives on a single test. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T17#GNS313_U2_T17_h4)

question: A clinic nurse partners with local agriculture officers to teach mothers about growing protein-rich crops. What strategy is this?

options.A: Passive immunization
options.B: Intersectoral collaboration
options.C: Tertiary rehabilitation
options.D: Appropriate technology

explanation: Working with agriculture to improve nutrition demonstrates collaboration between different sectors to promote community health. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T5#GNS124_U1_T5_h4)

question: What is the standard duration of unprotected intercourse required to clinically define infertility in couples under 35 years?

options.A: Twelve months
options.B: Six months
options.C: Eighteen months
options.D: Twenty-four months

explanation: Clinical guidelines establish twelve months of regular, unprotected intercourse as the threshold for investigating infertility in younger couples. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T19#GNS312_U1_T19_h1)

question: What is the primary danger associated with starting high-calorie nutrition too fast in starving patients?

options.A: Immediate development of chronic hypertension
options.B: Refeeding syndrome with dangerous electrolyte shifts
options.C: Sudden spikes in daily fluid elimination rates
options.D: Permanent loss of pancreatic enzyme production

explanation: Reintroducing calories quickly causes rapid cellular uptake of electrolytes, leading to severe deficiencies like low serum phosphate. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T009#GNS227_U6_T009_h6)

question: What is the primary focus of geriatric home healthcare nursing?

options.A: Transitioning every elderly patient into a nursing facility
options.B: Replacing the role of family caregivers completely
options.C: Curing all chronic degenerative diseases in the home
options.D: Maintaining independence and dignity in familiar environments

explanation: Home healthcare aims to keep older adults safe and autonomous in their own homes for as long as possible. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T3#GNS324_U3_T3_h1)

question: Which trophoblast derivative actively erodes the maternal endometrial stroma during the final stage of implantation?

options.A: Syncytiotrophoblast
options.B: Zona pellucida
options.C: Inner cell mass
options.D: Polar body

explanation: The multinucleated syncytiotrophoblast produces lytic enzymes that break down maternal tissue, allowing the embryo to bury deeply into the endometrium. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T2#GNS121_U6_T2_h3)

question: Which clinical condition is caused by a primary deficiency of dietary protein?

options.A: Kwashiorkor
options.B: Scurvy
options.C: Rickets
options.D: Beriberi

explanation: Kwashiorkor is a severe form of malnutrition driven specifically by inadequate protein intake despite adequate caloric intake. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T003#GNS227_U1_T003_h7)

question: The principle of unity of command in nursing management means what?

options.A: Staff report to only one designated supervisor
options.B: Management makes all clinical decisions alone
options.C: All nurses must work the same shift hours
options.D: Every ward must share the same equipment

explanation: Unity of command prevents confusion by ensuring an employee takes orders from and reports to a single supervisor. [learn more](GST321_U1_T13#GST321_U1_T13_h2)

question: Why is periodic re-assessment necessary in community health management?

options.A: To measure whether health interventions are improving the community
options.B: To prove that nurses are working overtime without pay
options.C: To satisfy the personal curiosity of visiting politicians
options.D: To increase the population size of the rural settlement

explanation: Repeating assessments helps track changes in health indices over time to evaluate program success. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T3#GNS124_U3_T3_h5)

question: What causes the body to stop making insulin in Type 1 diabetes?

options.A: Excessive placental hormone production
options.B: Autoimmune destruction of beta cells
options.C: Severe peripheral insulin resistance
options.D: Dietary deficiency of simple sugars

explanation: Type 1 diabetes occurs when the immune system attacks and destroys insulin-producing cells in the pancreas. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T13#GNS214_U1_T13_h2)

question: What does somaticization mean in the context of cultural expressions of emotional distress?

options.A: Psychiatric disorders are treated exclusively with herbal remedies
options.B: Depression is diagnosed purely through laboratory blood tests
options.C: Mental illness is openly discussed during community town halls
options.D: Emotional pain manifests as physical complaints like body heat or headaches

explanation: Somaticization occurs when psychological distress is experienced and communicated primarily through physical symptoms. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T7#GNS314_U1_T7_h4)

question: Which time horizon is characteristic of a long-term healthcare plan?

options.A: One week of duty rotation
options.B: Twenty-four to forty-eight hours
options.C: One to five years or more
options.D: One single nursing shift

explanation: Long-term plans project well into the future, spanning multiple years to achieve major milestones. [learn more](GST321_U1_T6#GST321_U1_T6_h5)

question: Which intervention is part of the active management of the third stage of labor?

options.A: Forcing early maternal ambulation
options.B: Performing an immediate episiotomy
options.C: Giving intravenous antibiotics
options.D: Administering a uterotonic drug

explanation: Giving a uterotonic like oxytocin immediately after delivery helps contract the uterus and prevent postpartum hemorrhage. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T004#GNS226_U1_T004_h4)

question: A client on combined oral contraceptives started taking new medications for seizures. What is the main clinical concern?

options.A: The pills will make the seizure medication poisonous
options.B: The combination will immediately cure all headaches
options.C: The seizure drugs can decrease contraceptive efficacy
options.D: The client will experience sudden weight loss overnight

explanation: Certain medications interact with hormonal contraceptives by speeding up their breakdown, which increases the risk of unintended pregnancy. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T024#GNS226_U6_T024_h6)

question: How much should daily energy intake increase for a symptomatic adult living with HIV?

options.A: 20 to 30 percent
options.B: 50 to 60 percent
options.C: No increase is needed
options.D: Exactly 5 percent

explanation: Symptomatic stages and infections demand higher calories to offset weight loss and metabolic stress. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T5#GNS216_U6_T5_h2)

question: When should hand hygiene be performed by a nurse in the clinical ward?

options.A: Before and after every direct patient contact
options.B: After completing all documentation tasks at the desk
options.C: Whenever hands look visibly soiled with dirt
options.D: Only at the beginning and end of the work shift

explanation: Regular hand hygiene breaks the chain of infection transmission between patients and healthcare workers. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T7#GNS122_U3_T7_h7)

question: What is the most critical infection control practice for caregivers performing home procedures?

options.A: Consistent and thorough hand hygiene
options.B: Wearing sterile surgical gowns all day
options.C: Boiling all household furniture weekly
options.D: Isolating the child in a locked room

explanation: Hand hygiene is the single most effective method for stopping the spread of microorganisms during home care procedures. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T11#GNS324_U3_T11_h6)

question: What is the primary purpose of wearing non-sterile gloves during patient care?

options.A: To completely eliminate the need for subsequent handwashing
options.B: To prevent allergic reactions to latex in patients
options.C: To protect the nurse from contact with infectious material
options.D: To ensure absolute sterility of the clinical environment

explanation: Gloves act as a barrier against blood and body fluids, though hand hygiene is still required after removal. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T9#GNS324_U6_T9_h3)

question: What role does the gallbladder play in managing bile between meals?

options.A: It adds digestive enzymes to neutralize incoming gastric chyme
options.B: It manufactures fresh bilirubin from worn-out red blood cells
options.C: It concentrates and stores bile until required for digestion
options.D: It filters bacteria out of the bile before it reaches the duodenum

explanation: The gallbladder absorbs water and electrolytes from hepatic bile, concentrating it and holding it safely until hormonal triggers prompt its release. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T5#GNS121_U1_T5_h4)

question: A midwife drops a used injection needle on the delivery room floor. What is the immediate safe action?

options.A: Drop it into a puncture-resistant safety box
options.B: Throw it into the general waste bin outside
options.C: Recap the needle carefully with both hands
options.D: Leave it on the floor for the cleaner

explanation: Sharps must be disposed of immediately into puncture-resistant boxes without recapping to prevent needle-stick injuries. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T4#GNS312_U5_T4_h4)

question: What is a common long-term problem caused by untreated heavy menstrual bleeding?

options.A: Chronic renal failure
options.B: Gestational diabetes mellitus
options.C: Iron-deficiency anemia
options.D: Obstructive airway disease

explanation: Ongoing excessive blood loss depletes iron stores, leading directly to iron-deficiency anemia. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T7#GNS311_U1_T7_h8)

question: A patient presents with a red, painful eye and thick purulent discharge. What nursing intervention is priority?

options.A: Preparing the patient for immediate laser surgery
options.B: Massaging the tear ducts every two hours
options.C: Teaching proper hand hygiene and infection control
options.D: Applying a tight eye patch to reduce movement

explanation: Infectious conjunctivitis spreads easily, making strict handwashing and hygiene essential to prevent outbreaks. [learn more](GNS311_U3_T3#GNS311_U3_T3_h3)

question: Why should a nurse NOT mention the incident report in the patient's clinical chart?

options.A: Incident reports are administrative tools kept separate from clinical charts
options.B: Doing so violates the privacy rights of the attending physician
options.C: Patients have the right to destroy incident reports legally
options.D: Chart space is too valuable for administrative notes

explanation: Incident reports are confidential internal documents intended for quality improvement, and keeping them out of the health record prevents legal confusion. [learn more](GST319_U6_T1#GST319_U6_T1_h6)

question: How does a vaccine primarily protect an individual against a specific infectious disease?

options.A: By stimulating the body's immune system to build resistance
options.B: By directly killing active pathogens circulating in the bloodstream
options.C: By coating the mucous membranes to block physical entry
options.D: By temporarily replacing the natural white blood cell count

explanation: Vaccines introduce antigens to trigger the immune system to produce antibodies and memory cells for future protection. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T12#GNS313_U2_T12_h1)

question: What does an echocardiogram mainly help doctors and nurses see?

options.A: Bacterial colonization on the inner myocardial lining
options.B: Circulating blood electrolyte and lipid concentrations
options.C: Electrical conduction pathways across the sinoatrial node
options.D: Heart valve structures and overall pumping efficiency

explanation: Echocardiography uses ultrasound imaging to evaluate heart anatomy, valve movement, and how well the heart pumps blood. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T2#GNS213_U1_T2_h5)
